BUG REPORT: "I have a command with a boolean flag that I marked as required:

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option('--on/--off', is_flag=True, required=True)
def cli(on):
    click.echo(on)
```

I expected that running `cli` with no arguments would stop with an error telling me the option is missing, since I declared it required. Instead the command runs anyway and prints `False`, so the required setting seems to be ignored for this flag."

Your job: find the root cause in /click/src/click (likely in core.py, the Option class / Option.consume_value / value_from_envvar / the parser), fix it minimally and correctly so that a required boolean flag (both the `--on/--off` secondary-flag form and the `is_flag=True` form) raises a UsageError ("Missing option ...") when it is not provided on the command line and has no envvar/default, while NOT breaking normal flag behavior (defaults, flag_value, envvar, prompts, `--help` output, `default=True` flags, etc.).

- Do NOT add new features. Minimal, targeted fix only.
- Do not touch unrelated code.

Verify: run the relevant test files, e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/test_options.py tests/test_basic.py tests/test_defaults.py tests/test_parser.py tests/test_commands.py tests/test_info_dict.py -q -p no:cacheprovider`, and also run the full suite `cd /click && python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` and report any failures (note: some failures may be pre-existing and unrelated - report them but do not try to fix them). BUG REPORT: "I use `click.Path(resolve_path=True)` for a CLI option, and when the path is a symlink whose target is a relative filename, the value I get back is wrong. I expect the absolute path of the real file, but instead I get a path based on my current working directory, so it points to a different location. For example:

```python
@click.command()
@click.option('--p', type=click.Path(resolve_path=True))
def cli(p):
    click.echo(p)
```

```console
$ mkdir -p /tmp/demo && cd /tmp/demo
$ touch real.txt
$ ln -s real.txt link
$ cd /
$ cli --p /tmp/demo/link
/real.txt        # I expected /tmp/demo/real.txt
```

Absolute symlink targets seem to resolve correctly; only relative ones come out wrong."

Your job: find the root cause in /click/src/click/types.py (the `Path` type's `convert`/`coerce_path_result`/`resolve_path` handling) and fix it minimally and correctly so that resolving a symlink whose target is relative yields the absolute path of the target resolved relative to the symlink's directory (e.g. `/tmp/demo/real.txt`), not relative to the current working directory. Note `os.path.realpath` already does the right thing; the bug is likely a manual `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), os.readlink(path))` style computation that mishandles relative link targets (e.g. joining with the dirname of the *resolved* path or using the wrong base). Keep behavior for absolute symlink targets, for `resolve_path` with non-symlinks, for `Path(exists=True)`/`file_okay`/`dir_okay` validation, and for relative input paths (they should still be made absolute relative to cwd) intact.

- Minimal, targeted fix only. Do not touch unrelated code. Other subagents may be editing other files (core.py, decorators.py, _compat.py, utils.py) concurrently - only edit /click/src/click/types.py.

Verify: write a reproduction script in /tmp (not in /click) that creates /tmp/demo/real.txt and /tmp/demo/link -> real.txt, chdirs to /, and calls the option conversion (e.g. via click.Path(resolve_path=True).convert or a CliRunner invocation) and shows it now returns /tmp/demo/real.txt (before the fix it returned /real.txt). Also test an absolute symlink target and a plain relative path. Then run `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/test_types.py tests/test_options.py tests/test_arguments.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` and the full suite `cd /click && python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`. Keep `click.option`/`click.argument` normal single-use behavior and `--help`/param order intact.

BUG REPORT: "I use a default map to turn a boolean flag on by default, but the help text doesn't reflect it. With this command:

```python
@click.command()
@click.option('--name/--no-name', is_flag=True, show_default=True)
def foo(name):
    click.echo(name)
```

running `foo` with `default_map={'foo': {'name': True}}` correctly prints `True`, yet `foo --help` still says `default: no-name`. I expected the help to say `default: name`, matching the value the flag actually takes. The help text seems to ignore the default map and only look at the flag's own default."

Your job: find the root cause in /click/src/click/core.py (look at `Option.get_help_record`, `Option.get_default`, `Parameter.get_default`, `Parameter.value_from_envvar`/`resolve_envvar_value`, and how `ctx.default_map` / `Context.lookup_default` is consulted) and fix it minimally and correctly so that when a `default_map` (or `default_map` on the context) supplies a value for an option, the `show_default` help text reflects the value that will actually be used - in particular for a boolean secondary flag (`--name/--no-name`) the help should show `default: name` when the default map says True and `default: no-name` when it says False, and for a normal option with a default_map value the shown default should be that value (formatted with the option's type). Keep behavior intact when there is no default_map, when the option has an explicit default, for `show_default` strings, `show_envvar`, `is_flag` single flags, and `--help` output formatting/width.

```python

click.echo('starting up')
```

I expected the output to just be dropped when there's no console attached, but instead I get `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'`."

The expected behavior is that output is silently discarded (e.g. writes go to a dummy/null stream) and reading from a missing stdin behaves sensibly (e.g. raises the usual click/EOF error rather than AttributeError).
